prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1214; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle struck the rear bumper while stopped at a red light. Both drivers exchanged information at the scene and a police report number was provided. Claimant reported neck stiffness at the scene and a wrist injury after the airbag deployed. Assigned for liability and injury review.

Entry 2: Contacted the claimant by phone to introduce myself and explain the claim process. Claimant confirmed she is not represented by an attorney and is handling the matter directly. Claimant describes wrist pain and limited grip in her right hand. She has been seen at an urgent care facility, where an X-ray was taken and a fracture of the wrist was diagnosed. Requested copies of all medical records and bills, and provided the authorization forms.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report. The responding officer noted the claimant's vehicle was stopped at the signal when the insured vehicle made contact at low speed. Officer cited the insured driver for following too closely. Photos from the scene show moderate rear damage to the claimant's vehicle and minor damage to the front of the insured vehicle. Liability appears clear, pending the insured's statement.

Entry 4: Took a recorded statement from the insured driver. He confirmed he was distracted by a phone call and did not notice traffic slowing ahead. He stated he did not dispute the citation. Vehicle has been inspected at the body shop, and the repair estimate has been received and is under review. Advised the insured that the claimant has an injury claim and that the insured should report any contact from the claimant's side.

Entry 5: Received the medical records from the claimant's provider. Diagnosis confirmed as a fracture of the distal radius, treated with a splint and referral to an orthopedic specialist. Follow-up appointment is scheduled. Claimant has not yet returned to work full time. Sent a letter to the claimant explaining the next steps, including the need for a final medical update before settlement can be evaluated. Diary set for follow-up in two weeks.
